key_insight: MRI radiomic features improved survival prediction beyond clinical variables in lung cancer brain metastases and were associated with tumor immune features.
clinical_relevance: Combining MRI biomarkers with clinical information could refine prognostic risk stratification, pending further validation.
method: Retrospective analysis of 103 patients with matched preoperative MRI and histopathology.
Combined contrast-enhanced T1 and T2-FLAIR radiomics with clinical variables in Cox, random survival forest, and DeepSurv models.
Evaluated overall survival, CNS progression, and leptomeningeal progression; compared imaging-only risk groups with immune features.
evidence_signal: The combined clinical-imaging DeepSurv model achieved the highest overall-survival concordance index (0.728); endpoint-specific risk groups differed significantly in overall survival and leptomeningeal progression, but not CNS progression.
watch_item: The small retrospective cohort limits generalizability; independent prospective validation is needed before clinical use.
paper_title: MRI Biomarkers for Brain Metastases in Lung Cancer Using Machine Learning
